query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small amount of zirconium (approximately 1–2 atomic %) to the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy will improve its load-bearing integrity (by enhancing yield strength and fracture toughness) without degrading its significant caloric effect under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy in its as-synthesized form, exhibiting high caloric performance but poor load-bearing integrity and a tendency to crack.
generation.intervention: Introduce a microalloying addition of approximately 1–2 atomic % zirconium (Zr) during alloy processing.
generation.conditions: Evaluated under operating refrigeration conditions including applied magnetic and pressure fields in the temperature range relevant to the caloric operation (e.g., near room temperature or refrigeration performance temperatures) and under mechanical load relevant for load-bearing applications.
generation.structural_mediator: The large atomic size of Zr will create localized lattice distortion and may promote the formation of finely dispersed intermetallic phases that act as obstacles to dislocation motion, thus enhancing the mechanical integrity of the alloy.
generation.mechanism: The excessive atomic size difference introduced by Zr increases lattice strain and solid solution strengthening, thereby improving yield strength and resistance to crack propagation. Because the caloric response in these alloys is largely governed by field-induced phase transitions and magneto-structural responses, a modest Zr addition is anticipated to influence the mechanical microstructure while leaving the caloric phase transition largely intact.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Zr-doped alloy will exhibit improved load-bearing properties (e.g., higher yield strength and fracture toughness, reduced cracking) while maintaining a caloric response comparable to the undoped alloy under similar applied magnetic and pressure fields.
generation.baseline: The original (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, which shows high caloric effects but suffers from poor mechanical integrity and cracking.
generation.boundary: The intervention is expected to be effective within the operational regime of applied-field and pressure-field induced caloric cooling at near-room or refrigeration temperatures and under mechanical loading conditions typical for refrigeration device components.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal Zr concentration that maximizes mechanical reinforcement without adversely affecting the caloric phase transition is not precisely known. There is also uncertainty whether any secondary phase formation induced by Zr might subtly influence the caloric response.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of the standard (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy and one set with 1–2 atomic % Zr added during synthesis. Ensure identical processing conditions for both sets. Conduct compression tests and fracture toughness measurements to assess load-bearing integrity. Simultaneously, perform caloric effect measurements (such as entropy change and adiabatic temperature change) under applied magnetic and pressure fields at the operational temperature.
measurements: Yield strength and fracture toughness from mechanical compression tests.
Strain-to-failure and crack propagation behavior from microscopic observations.
Caloric response parameters (e.g., isothermal entropy change, adiabatic temperature change) under similar field and pressure conditions as used in refrigeration applications.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Zr-doped samples do not show a statistically significant improvement (e.g., >10% increase) in mechanical integrity (yield strength, fracture toughness) compared to the baseline, or if the caloric performance (entropy change or temperature change) is reduced by more than about 10% relative to the undoped alloy, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Moreover, the addition of Zr can form an excessive atomic size difference (δ) with other elements and cause lattice distortion due to its large atomic radius, which can promote the formation of intermetallic compounds, resulting in the enhancement of mechanical properties []. Based on above, novel Wx(TaVZr)100−x RHEAs were designed and prepared. The effects of various W contents on their microstructural characteristics and compressive mechanical properties were systematically investigated. The underlying mechanisms for the phase formation and strengthening of the RHEAs were also examined and discussed.
